NFL DFS Projections Week 6: DraftKings Picks, Values and Sim Plays

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, October 18 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 16, 9:32 AM ET

Bijan Robinson carries the highest SPAGS model projection on the Week 6 DraftKings main slate: 25.4 DraftKings points at $8,700. He holds 27% of the simulated winning-lineup credit across 10,000 simulations. Puka Nacua holds the largest share at 33% for $8,100.

Behind Robinson, the model's next four projections are Kenneth Walker III (25.1, $8,500), Josh Allen (22.7, $7,500), Puka Nacua (21.9, $8,100) and Kyren Williams (21.7, $6,800). Kyren Williams returns the most per dollar of that group at 3.19 projected points per $1,000. Puka Nacua leads the wide receivers at 21.9 for $8,100, Josh Allen leads the quarterbacks at 22.7 for $7,500, and Brock Bowers leads the tight ends at 18.6 for $7,500.

The 10-game slate runs from a 53.5-point total in BUF at LV down to 38.5 in CAR at PHI. Every projection below is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 16, 9:32 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. Winning-lineup credit comes from 10,000 simulations of the contest, and tied winning entries share credit. A player's simulated floor is his 10th-percentile score and his ceiling is his 95th.

Quarterbacks: Week 6 DraftKings projections

Josh Allen, BUF at LV ($7,500)

Josh Allen carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 22.7 DraftKings points at $7,500, the 3rd-highest on the entire main slate. That is 1.2 points clear of Matthew Stafford. The model includes 6.8 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 3.03 projected points per $1,000, 13th of 17 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Allen averaged 22.8 points with a simulated floor of 9.5 and a ceiling of 41.4, and he holds 10% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Buffalo is a 4.5-point favorite on the road against Las Vegas, with an implied team total of 29 in a game totaled at 53.5.

Matthew Stafford, LAR vs ARI ($6,400)

Matthew Stafford projects 2nd at the position with 21.4 DraftKings points at $6,400. The salary works out to 3.35 projected points per $1,000, 5th of 17 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Stafford averaged 21.3 points with a simulated floor of 8.3 and a ceiling of 39.8, and he holds 16% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. The Rams are a 12.5-point favorite at home against Arizona, with an implied team total of 32 in a game totaled at 51.5.

Value: Deshaun Watson, CLE vs BAL ($4,900)

Deshaun Watson projects for 17.4 DraftKings points at $4,900, which works out to 3.54 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 17 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. The model includes 7.2 rushing attempts. Across 10,000 simulations Watson averaged 17.5 points with a simulated floor of 7.0 and a ceiling of 31.7, and he holds 6% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Cleveland is a 3.5-point underdog at home against Baltimore, with an implied team total of 18.5 in a game totaled at 40.5.
